summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with a B.E. in Electronics and Telecommunication and hands-on embedded firmware experience across STM32 Cortex-M4, Arduino/AVR, and Linux-based platforms. Writes low-level, real-time firmware in C, programming peripherals directly at the register level (GPIO, timers, ADC, I2C) and building interrupt-driven device drivers for multi-sensor hardware. Experienced in UART, I2C, and SPI interfacing, PCB design in EAGLE, and debugging firmware and hardware interactions with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C on a Cortex-M4 (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) including a hand-written low-level I2C driver; 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture for real-time temperature sensing and display; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override on STM32.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing over I2C and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Designed a three-layer system communication fabric over a unified WebSocket link, with a USB-serial link from the Linux edge host down to the microcontroller.
Implemented two-link IK in C++ on an Arduino controller driving five servos; interfaced dual VL53L0X time-of-flight sensors through a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer for a 25 mm contact-aware grasp trigger.
Resolved 11 firmware and hardware integration failures (servo brown-out, stale-frame capture, serial reconnect); achieved 100% pick reliability across 10 trials.
